name: Meridian House Style
description: House style for the fictional agency Meridian. Formal-professional analyst-report register. This is the rubric the twenty-document memory-off vs memory-on curve is measured against. Fictional client; all corpus documents are fabricated.

counting.record_uncapped_note: The checker MUST emit both `count_capped` (min(raw, 5)) and `count_raw` (uncapped) per rule per document. The cap prevents a single runaway rule from dominating the correction count; the raw count preserves the true magnitude of an early improvement, which the cap would otherwise silently compress. Both are reported in the write-up.
reporting_split: deterministic_subset: H1, H2, H4, H5, H6, H7, H8, H9, H10, H11, H12, H13, H14 (13 rules, no model call)
counting.reporting_split_note: Headline curve is reported for the deterministic subset and for the full set separately, so the noisiest rule cannot be mistaken for the signal.

checker_contract.blinding_note: The checker process receives only document text and a rubric id. It is never passed the arm label (memory on/off), the run id, the document ordinal, the client id, or any prior score. Documents are submitted to the checker in a shuffled order with opaque content-hash filenames so the arm cannot be inferred from ordering or naming.
checker_contract.prompt_change_policy: A checker prompt is immutable once a real run has used it. Any change requires a new version file (e.g. h3_passive_v2.md), a new checker_prompt_version value here, a new rubric version, and re-scoring of all prior documents with the new version before any cross-version comparison is made. Mixed-version scores are never compared.

rules.rule: Oxford comma required in lists of three or more items.
rules.counting_unit: each list that omits the serial comma
rules.guard: Suppress when the comma is sentence-initial adverbial (match starts within the first 3 words of the sentence) or is followed by a clause containing a finite verb on both sides of the conjunction.
rules.false_positive_notes: Fires on 'In 2020, revenue and costs rose' (adverbial comma, not a list) and on compound predicates. Guard above reduces but does not eliminate this. Fixture tests in tests/fixtures/h1_*.txt must pin both the true-positive and the known false-positive shapes before this rule is used in a scored run.

violation: We reviewed scope, budget and timeline.
compliant: We reviewed scope, budget, and timeline.

rules.rule: Headings use sentence case: first word and proper nouns capitalized, nothing else.
rules.procedure: For each heading node: tokenize on whitespace. A violation is recorded if any token after the first begins with an uppercase letter and is not in proper_noun_allowlist and is not fully uppercase acronym of length 2-5.
rules.false_positive_notes: Proper nouns outside the allowlist will false-positive. The allowlist is fixed at rubric version time and covers every proper noun appearing in the committed corpus; corpus generation must not introduce proper nouns absent from the list.

compliant: ## Reviewing the Q3 numbers for Meridian

rules.false_positive_notes: The be-verb + past-participle heuristic over-fires on adjectival participles ('is required', 'was founded in 1997') and on legitimate agentless passives. This is the noisiest rule in the rubric and the only one requiring a model call. Its per-document contribution is reported as its own column so the curve can be read with and without it.

violation: The report was approved by the committee.

rules.rule: Spell out zero through nine; use numerals for 10 and above; always use numerals when the number is paired with a unit of measure.
rules.procedure: Violation if (a) a numeral 0-9 appears in prose with no unit token within the next three tokens, or (b) a number word for ten or above appears in prose, or (c) a number word zero-nine is immediately followed by a unit token.

rules.rule: Write 'percent' in prose. The % symbol is not used in body text.
rules.pattern_note: Matches the whole number, not just the digit before the symbol. The narrower \d\s*% reported a span of '0%' for a '30%' violation; spans are quoted verbatim into correction messages, so a truncated span degrades every correction built on it. Count is unaffected. Pinned by tests/fixtures/h5_span.md.

rules.rule: Dates are written 13 August 2026. No ordinals, no slashes, no month-first ordering.
Citations are inline parenthetical (Author, Year). Bare URLs do not appear in body text.
rules.counting_unit: each bare URL, plus each citation-like construct not matching (Author, Year)
rules.procedure: Count every bare_url match. Then count every citation_like match that is not also a wellformed_citation match.

rules.guard: Exclude possessive 's on nouns: suppress when the token before 's is a capitalized noun or is followed by a noun and the sentence has no auxiliary reading. Possessive/contraction disambiguation for 's is documented as a known imperfection; corpus generation avoids possessive 's to keep this rule clean.
rules.false_positive_notes: Possessive 's is the only ambiguous case. Corpus documents are generated without possessive 's so that this rule is exact on the measured set.

violation: It's ready and we don't expect delays.
compliant: It is ready and we do not expect delays.

rules.procedure: Split on sentence-final punctuation followed by whitespace and a capital letter, with an abbreviation exception list. Count whitespace-delimited tokens containing at least one alphanumeric character. Violation if count > 30.

violation: We leverage a robust, seamless workflow.

rules.rule: Parenthetical breaks use an unspaced em dash. Spaced hyphens, double hyphens, and spaced en dashes are not used.
Bullet items begin with a capital letter and carry no terminal punctuation.
rules.procedure: For each list item: violation if the first alphabetic character is lowercase, or if the item ends in . ! ? ; or :. One violation per item even if both halves fail.

rules.rule: Acronyms are expanded on first use with the acronym in parentheses; bare thereafter.
rules.counting_unit: each acronym whose first occurrence in the document is unexpanded
rules.procedure: Find all tokens matching [A-Z]{2,5} that are not in the never_expand list. For each distinct acronym, locate its first occurrence; violation if it is not immediately preceded by an expansion of the form 'Words Words (ACRONYM)'.

compliant: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) grew this year.

rules.rule: Person: 'we' for the firm, 'you' for the reader. Never 'I', never 'one' as a pronoun, never 'the reader'.

banned_patterns.note: case-sensitive: lowercase 'i' is not the pronoun

violation: I recommend that one should review the draft.
compliant: We recommend that you review the draft.

changes: H14 banned_patterns become objects carrying their own case sensitivity. The patterns were matched case-sensitively, so a sentence-initial 'The reader' or 'One should' was missed while mid-sentence occurrences counted. '\\bI\\b' must stay case-sensitive (lowercase 'i' is not a violation), so a blanket IGNORECASE was not available. Found by the injector round-trip; pinned by tests/fixtures/h14_sentence_initial.md.
No scored run has used any earlier version, so no re-scoring is owed.

H4 (a): the unit token may now be separated from the numeral by up to two modifiers ('5 business days'). Requiring adjacency turned compliant numerals-with-units prose into violations. Found against real model prose; pinned by tests/fixtures/h4_unit_gap.md.
No scored run has used any earlier version, so no re-scoring is owed.
H5 pattern widened to match the whole number, not the digit adjacent to the symbol. Counts unaffected; spans are quoted into correction messages and a '30%' violation was reporting '0%'.
H13 never_expand gains IT, alongside US/UK/EU/AI/CEO/PDF/URL. 'Information Technology (IT)' is pedantic beyond the list's stated intent. Found when real model prose wrote 'the IT department'.
No scored run has used version 1.0.0, so no re-scoring is owed.
